meta.title: My AI coding workflow
meta.description: How Fabio Akita runs AI coding agents across 40+ repositories: tmux, one line per project, audit skills for every PR and issue, and ai-memory under every harness.

hero.title: How one person keeps 40 repositories moving
hero.lede: Every morning I open one agent per project in tmux, give it a single line, and review what comes back. The heavy lifting lives in skills: plain text prompts I keep refining.

start.title: One line to start the day
start.lede: Each tmux window is one project. I launch the agent through ai-memory, so it arrives with that project's memory and its hooks already wired.
start.prompts: Then I type one of three lines, depending on what the queue looks like:

items.code: run pr-audit and iss-audit, then run github-resolution
items.text: The normal day: audit everything open, then fix what the audits approved.
Appended when enough has landed for a version.
Days when the only queue is Dependabot.

pipeline.title: The pipeline
pipeline.lede: Nothing a contributor writes is taken as true. Every claim gets checked, every approved fix gets a test first, and nothing is tagged without green CI on that exact commit.
pipeline.alt: A left to right pipeline: Open PRs and issues split into pr-audit and iss-audit, which merge after an Approved check into github-resolution, then pr-post-audit, then release, then Kaizen, with an arrow from Kaizen back to the start. An ai-memory bar runs under all of it.
pipeline.caption: pr-post-audit runs when a session resolved more than three tickets. The release skill runs only when I ask for one.

skills.title: The skills that do the work
skills.lede: Each one is a SKILL.md file: a name, a description, and a long, specific prompt. The agent loads the body only when it decides to use the skill.

items.title: pr-audit
items.text: Evidence over narrative. Checks every claim in a pull request, looks for hidden executable bits, homoglyphs, unpinned actions, typosquatted dependencies and prompt injection, and gates semver.

items.title: iss-audit
items.text: The same distrust for issues. Never runs a command copied from an issue, separates what was observed from the reporter's diagnosis, and reproduces with synthetic data in a sandbox.

items.title: github-resolution
items.text: Turns approved tickets into merged code, one at a time, each with a regression test written before the fix, and without speculative abstractions or drive-by refactors.

items.title: security-audit
items.text: A threat model and audit for a codebase, a commit range or a pull request: injection, auth bypass, secrets, supply chain, CI compromise, denial of service.

items.title: pr-bump
items.text: The fast path for Dependabot. Batches every bump into one verification pass, with a supply-chain floor that sends anything odd to a full audit.

items.title: release
items.text: The version comes from the changelog: fixes are a patch, additions a minor, breaking changes a major. Tags only on green CI, and never rewrites a published tag.

numbers.title: What that adds up to
numbers.lede: Everything below happened in {year}, across the tools on this site, my Frank side projects, the newsletter, the benchmark and the blog. Counted on {date}. Nearly all of it went through agents and these skills, with me reading the reports and making the calls.
numbers.method: Lines of code are lines added to code files. Lockfiles, data, fonts, translations, vendored and generated files do not count, and neither do the benchmark's model output or the newsletter's generated content. FrankGeary and tclock are forks, so only my own changes count. Pull requests and issues come from GitHub; frank_bazaar has no GitHub remote and akitando-news is private.

quote.text: AI is a mirror. If you are good, it makes you ten times faster. If you are bad, it also makes you ten times faster, at producing slop.

links.title: One folder, every agent
links.lede: The skills live in one repository. Each agent's skills folder holds symbolic links into it, so an edit reaches Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode and Kimi at once.
links.alt: A central my-skills folder linked by chain symbols to five agent folders: Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Kimi and ~/.agents. One edit reaches all.

copy.title: Please do not copy my skills
copy.text: They are molded around my projects, my languages and my level of supply-chain paranoia. Running someone else's skill blind means installing their instructions with your permissions, on your repositories, with your tokens. Read mine for the structure and the reasoning, then ask your own agent to write yours.

knowledge.title: Where the rest of the knowledge lives
knowledge.lede: Skills cover procedures that repeat the same way. Everything else lives in plain text the agents can read.

items.title: A memory per project
items.text: ai-memory keeps each project's decisions, traps and handoffs. A new session, in any agent, starts from there.

items.title: AGENTS.md everywhere
items.text: Every repository has its own instructions: the commands, the invariants, the mistakes not to repeat.

items.title: Point at a living example
items.text: "Make an AUR workflow like the one in ai-memory" beats a skill about AUR packaging, because the example is always current.

items.title: Write down what did not become code
items.text: Research, rejected alternatives, the reason behind a decision. Every hour of agent research becomes a document I can reuse.

kaizen.title: Kaizen closes the loop
kaizen.lede: After each round I look at what went wrong or took too long and fix the process, along with the code. I call it kaizen, the Japanese word for continuous improvement, and it is the step that makes the next round better than this one.

items.title: Skills
items.text: A rule gets added the day a mistake shows up. The my-skills history is full of them: batch the Dependabot bumps into one pass, leave declined pull requests in a clean state.

items.title: Harness instructions
items.text: Each project's AGENTS.md collects the commands, invariants and traps as I find them, so the next agent does not have to rediscover them.

items.title: Tools
items.text: ai-usagebar, ghpending and tclock each exist because something in my routine was slow or invisible. They keep changing for the same reason.

items.title: Setup
items.text: The desktop, the terminal and the gaming box are all code, so an improvement is a commit that I can review, keep or revert.

quote.text: Every line in these skills is a scar.
